messages:
clare: quick heads up: saw phone numbers in EXIF on sampled traces for /v1/respond. not huge volume but definitely PII.
ops-bot: alert: attachments.exif.pii_hits route=/v1/respond count=2 in 8m :warning:
oscar: how are attachments handled today? i thought we treated blobs opaque unless debug header set.
clare: yes, opaque by default. canary had `x-debug-inspect:1` enabled which let the collector persist full EXIF.
mina: that's a policy hole. debug headers must never enable raw attachment retention in canaries or prod. we need an ingress enforcement to block debug header unless tenant is in dev allowlist.
devx: UX idea: add a quarantine action on the sample row that replaces blob with a placeholder and writes fingerprint metadata. also show a sticky audit note about who quarantined it.
oscar: agree. implementation: server-side job should rewrite the object (strip EXIF) and store `fingerprint = sha256(image)+route+ts` in the sample row. no raw EXIF anywhere.
mina: telemetry: add metrics `attachments.exif.pii_hits`, `attachments.quarantine.count`, and `attachments.quarantine.forensics_requests`. sample table should only store hashed fingerprints and pseudonym tokens, never raw values.
clare: fallback behaviour: if scrub fails, don't store raw text. pseudonymize locally with tenant-scoped HMAC and store `[ATT:<12hex>]` token and mark `telemetry.redact_status=pseudonymized`.
oscar: code sketch for fallback: `token = hmac_sha256(kms_key_for_tenant, field_value)[:12]` and store `ATT:` prefix. keys from KMS, rotated monthly.
devx: console: add "Quarantine & Scrub" action and an emergency "Strip-all" route toggle (ops-only, RBAC + audit). the strip-all flips `inspect.mode=strip-all` for route and replaces new samples with placeholders.
mina: runbook tweak: auto-quarantine if attachments.exif.pii_hits > 3/min for a route, and escalate to security. ops-bot can enact quarantine rule temporarily.
ops-bot: rule added: auto-quarantine threshold=3/min target=/v1/respond :white_check_mark:
oscar: tests: unit for header block on canary, integration to ensure quarantine rewrites blob and keeps fingerprint, property test to ensure pseudonym tokens are non-reversible and truncated.
clare: legal check: confirm storing truncated pseudonym token is allowed without extra consent. filing with privacy.
devx: small feature-flag example for console: { "route": "/v1/respond", "feature": "attachments.quarantine", "state": "on", "roles": ["ops","sec"] }
mina: follow-ups: I'll open RFC for attachment quarantine + pseudonymize fallback with metrics and console flows. target review in 72h.
oscar: I'll add unit tests and block debug headers in canary ingress.
clare: thanks team, immediate mitigation with auto-quarantine in place. will close after RFC lands. :thumbsup:
